mainTopic: פיגול and the מתירין: the יום הכיפורים sprinklings, the count of blood placements, half a מתיר in a מנחה, and items with no פיגול liability
overview: This amud opens by closing a challenge against רב אשי: his reading of the ברייתא does not fit its wording 'whether... whether,' and the difficulty stands. The גמרא then returns to the same ברייתא, where רבי מאיר says an improper thought during one set of the יום הכיפורים sprinklings makes the offering פיגול with כרת. It asks how this can be, since כרת requires that all the מתירין were done, and a ruined sprinkling inside should turn the later sprinklings into plain water. רבה answers that the case has four bulls and four goats. רבא answers that even with one bull and one goat, the improper sprinkling still counts for making the offering פיגול. Next the גמרא explains why different ברייתות count 43, 47, or 48 blood placements: each follows a different opinion about mixing the blood for the corners and about whether the leftover blood is required. The גמרא then challenges ריש לקיש's view of רבי מאיר from a ברייתא about a מנחה, where רבי מאיר rules פיגול even when only the frankincense had the improper thought. An attempt to reread that ברייתא fails, and the difficulty remains. Finally a new משנה begins listing items that carry no כרת for פיגול, starting with the קומץ, the קטורת, and the לבונה.

steps.title: The wording 'whether... whether' does not fit רב אשי's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's explanation from the wording of the ברייתא, which says 'whether in this set, whether in that set.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's explanation by pointing to the actual words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי explained the ברייתא as a case where the כהן גדול had an improper thought during every set of sprinklings. But the ברייתא says 'whether during the first set, whether during the second,' which means even one set with a bad thought is enough. So רב אשי's reading does not match the text.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, doesn't it... (opens a challenge)
whether... whether (either one alone)
it teaches (in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'whether... whether'!
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא's words: whether during this set of sprinklings, whether during that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from before this section, challenging רב אשי's explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's explanation that the improper thought was present in all the sets of sprinklings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording 'whether... whether' shows that a bad thought in any single set is enough. That contradicts a reading that needs it in all of them.

steps.title: The challenge stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the difficulty against רב אשי is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer for this challenge, and it closes this line of discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קשיא' means the question remains a real problem. רב אשי's reading is left weakened but is not formally rejected as a law. The גמרא now moves on.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult; the question stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' here is not a new question. It is the גמרא's verdict that the question just asked has no answer.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge raised in step 1 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אשי's explanation does not fit the ברייתא's wording, and the difficulty remains.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר: the offering is פיגול with כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes רבי מאיר. An improper thought in one set of the inner sprinklings makes the offering פיגול with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: רבי מאיר says it is פיגול, and one is liable to כרת for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about the יום הכיפורים sprinklings and quotes רבי מאיר's ruling, so it can examine it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a bad thought during just one set of sprinklings. רבי מאיר says that alone makes the whole offering פיגול, so anyone who eats it gets כרת. The next steps will question how this is possible.

keyTerms.meaning: an offering ruined by a thought of eating or burning it beyond its proper time
spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: The master said,
Rabbi Meir says: it is piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to a different line of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a bad thought in one set of the inner sprinklings makes the offering פיגול with כרת.

steps.title: The rule: no כרת unless all the מתירין were offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays down a known principle. פיגול with כרת happens only if all the מתירין were done, just like a valid offering only works after all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, one is not liable to כרת until all its permitting parts have been offered. The master said: a disqualified offering works like a valid one. A valid offering is accepted only once all its permitting parts are offered, and a disqualified offering also becomes פיגול only once all its permitting parts are offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It first states a basic rule that it will use against רבי מאיר in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An offering becomes פיגול only if everything that makes it 'work' was completed. This is the same requirement a good offering needs in order to be accepted. So if any required sprinkling is missing, there is no פיגול and no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: now, consider (opens a reasoning setup)
its permitting parts (the services that make the offering effective)
acceptance; the offering 'working'
valid / disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the foundation of all the laws of פיגול: a bad thought only counts once the whole service has been finished.

phrases.english: Now, one is not liable to karet
until all its permitting parts have been offered –
as the master said:
like the acceptance of a valid offering, so is the 'acceptance' of a disqualified one;
phrases.notes: For the disqualified offering, 'acceptance' means it actually takes on the status of פיגול.

phrases.english: just as the acceptance of a valid offering –
happens only once all its permitting parts have been offered,
so too the 'acceptance' of a disqualified one –
happens only once all its permitting parts have been offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי כָּרֵת לָא מִיחַיַּיב עַד שֶׁיִּקְרְבוּ כׇּל מַתִּירָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in a known principle as the first half of a challenge to רבי מאיר's ruling in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול with כרת requires that all the מתירין of the offering were completed.

steps.title: A disqualified inner sprinkling makes the later sprinklings worthless
steps.stepSummary: The improper thought inside the קודש הקדשים ruins that sprinkling, so the later sprinklings in the היכל are like sprinkling water. Then the מתירין were never completed, so how can there be כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since he had the bad thought while sprinkling inside, the sprinkling is disqualified, and it is as if he did not sprinkle at all. So when he goes on to sprinkle in the היכל, he is just sprinkling water!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the rule from the previous step to challenge רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים every set of inner sprinklings is required. If the first set inside was ruined by a bad thought, the blood was never properly sprinkled. The blood he uses afterward no longer counts as real blood for the offering. So the מתירין were never completed, and by the rule in step 4 there should be no פיגול and no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: inside (in the קודש הקדשים)
it is as if he did not sprinkle
the Sanctuary, outside the קודש הקדשים
just plain water

phrases.english: But since he had an improper thought with it
inside, it is disqualified –
it is as if he did not sprinkle;
when he then sprinkles in the Sanctuary –
it is merely water that he is sprinkling!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כֵּיוָן דְּחַשֵּׁיב בֵּיהּ בִּפְנִים פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from step 4 against רבי מאיר's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a bad thought in one set of sprinklings brings פיגול with כרת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruined first sprinkling means the later sprinklings do not count. Then the מתירין were never completed, and without that there can be no פיגול.

steps.title: רבה: the case has four bulls and four goats
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that each set of sprinklings was done with blood from a new bull and goat. So no later set relies on blood that was already ruined.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: You can find this case with four bulls and four goats.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by describing a specific case where רבי מאיר's ruling works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture this: after each set of sprinklings was done with a bad thought, the leftover blood spilled. A new bull and goat were then brought for the next set. Each set used fresh blood and was completed as a set, so every מתיר was really done. The rule from step 4 is then satisfied, and פיגול with כרת can apply.

keyTerms.meaning: you can find it (a case where the ruling works)
bulls
goats

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול needs all the מתירין to be completed. In the יום הכיפורים case, רבה makes this possible by using a new bull and goat for each of the four sets of sprinklings, while רבא (next step) says even one bull and goat is enough, because the improper sprinkling still counts for פיגול.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
You can find it
with four bulls and four goats.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling is set in a specific situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that one set of blood was used for all the sprinklings, so a ruined first set would make the later sets worthless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each set used fresh blood from a new animal, so every מתיר was completed and פיגול with כרת applies.

steps.title: רבא: Even one bull and goat works for פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question differently. Even with only one bull and one goat, the sprinkling done with the improper thought still counts as done for the purpose of making the offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say it was one bull and one goat. The sprinkling 'works' for making it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from step 5, without needing רבה's idea of a new bull and goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that the ruined sprinkling makes the later ones like water, so the מתירין were never finished. רבא says the improper sprinkling is not 'nothing' when it comes to פיגול. It counts as a real step toward making the offering פיגול, so when the כהן finishes all the sprinklings, all the מתירין count as done for פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (the answer works even in the harder case)
The bull and the goat brought on יום כפור
It 'works' for its פיגול: it counts as done in order to make the offering פיגול

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the offering is kosher. It is ruined. He only says the sprinkling still counts as done, so it can make the offering פיגול with כרת.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּפַר אֶחָד וְשָׂעִיר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: You can even say it was with one bull and one goat,
for its piggul, it effects acceptance.
phrases.notes: He means the sprinkling still counts as a real act when it comes to making the offering פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question in step 5, different from רבה's answer in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the problem: the ruined sprinkling still counts for פיגול
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After a ruined sprinkling, the later sprinklings are like water, so the מתירין are never complete and there can be no כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the purpose of פיגול, the sprinkling with the improper thought counts as done, so all the מתירין are complete even with one bull and one goat.

steps.title: Forty-three or forty-seven placements?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא said there are forty-three blood placements on יום כפור. Another ברייתא says forty-seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said 'forty-three.' But another ברייתא teaches forty-seven!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the number in the ברייתא and points out that a different ברייתא gives a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty-three is 8 placements each for the bull and the goat inside the קודש הקדשים, and the same again toward the פרוכת in the היכל (32), plus 4 on the corners of the inner מזבח, plus 7 on top of it. A second ברייתא counts forty-seven, four more, so the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא), introducing a contradiction
Forty-three: the count of blood placements in our ברייתא

phrases.english: Forty-three.
phrases.notes: These are the words of our ברייתא that the גמרא now discusses.

phrases.english: But it was taught: forty-seven!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the פיגול question and turns to the number of placements in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's count of forty-three placements
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא counts forty-seven. The two numbers cannot both be right unless something explains the difference.

steps.title: The difference: mixing the blood for the corners
steps.stepSummary: Forty-three follows the view that the bull's and goat's blood are mixed before going on the corners. Forty-seven follows the view that they are not mixed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one follows the view that they mix the blood for the corners, and that one follows the view that they do not mix for the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each ברייתא follows a different opinion about the corners of the inner מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood is mixed first, there are only 4 placements on the corners, which gives forty-three. If each animal's blood goes on the corners by itself, there are 4 + 4 = 8, which gives four more, forty-seven.

keyTerms.meaning: This follows the one who says
They mix (the blood of the bull and the goat together)
The corners of the inner (gold) מזבח

phrases.english: This follows the one who says they mix for the corners,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְעָרְבִין לַקְּרָנוֹת.
phrases.english: and that follows the one who says they do not mix for the corners.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seem to argue about the actual number of placements for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference comes from a known argument about whether the blood is mixed before it goes on the corners.

steps.title: A third count: forty-eight
steps.stepSummary: Yet another ברייתא counts forty-eight placements, one more than forty-seven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא with yet another number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after explaining forty-three and forty-seven, a ברייתא saying forty-eight needs an explanation for one more placement.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty-eight: a third count of the placements

phrases.english: But it was taught: forty-eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 9 explained forty-seven, a new source gives an even higher number.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A third ברייתא counts forty-eight, so there is one more placement that still needs an explanation.

steps.title: The difference: is pouring out the leftover blood required?
steps.stepSummary: Forty-eight follows the view that pouring the leftover blood is required, so it is counted. Forty-seven follows the view that it is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one follows the view that the leftovers are required, and that one follows the view that the leftovers are not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the extra placement by pointing to another argument, about the leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the sprinklings, the leftover blood is poured on the base of the outer מזבח. If that pouring is required for the service to work, it is counted as one more placement, giving forty-eight. If it is not required, it is not counted, giving forty-seven.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover blood, poured on the base of the outer מזבח
Are required: without them the service does not work

steps.whatToRemember: The three counts (43, 47, 48) do not argue about the facts for no reason. Each comes from a known argument: mixing for the corners (adds 4), and whether the leftover blood is required (adds 1).

phrases.english: This follows the one who says the leftovers are required,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין שִׁירַיִים מְעַכְּבִין.
phrases.english: that follows the one who says the leftovers are not required.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forty-seven and forty-eight look like a plain contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra one is the pouring of the leftover blood, which is counted only by the view that it is required.

steps.title: A ברייתא about פיגול in a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge from a ברייתא about a מנחה. It lists the steps where an improper thought makes it פיגול: taking the handful, putting it in a כלי, and walking it to the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: When is this said? With the taking of the handful, with putting it in a כלי, and with walking it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It begins quoting a ברייתא about the מנחה, and the actual question comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the steps of a מנחה where an improper thought can make it פיגול. The challenge is aimed at ריש לקיש's view of רבי מאיר, that half of a מתיר cannot make an offering פיגול. The ברייתא will be used to test that view.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said?
Taking the handful of flour from a מנחה
Putting the handful into a holy כלי
Walking the handful to the מזבח

phrases.english: They challenged:
phrases.notes: The challenge is against ריש לקיש's view of רבי מאיר, that half a מתיר cannot make פיגול.

phrases.english: In what case is this said?
With the taking of the handful, with putting it in a כלי, and with walking it;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the count of placements and goes back to the question of פיגול in half a מתיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's understanding of רבי מאיר, that an improper thought in half a מתיר does not make פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the מנחה lists the steps where an improper thought makes פיגול. The full challenge, built on this list, comes in the lines that follow.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: improper thought during only the handful or only the frankincense
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא from step 12 continues. If the improper thought was only during the burning of the קומץ or only during the burning of the לבונה, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול with כרת. חכמים say there is no כרת unless the thought covered the whole מתיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when he gets to the burning: if he put the handful on the fire with an improper thought and the frankincense in silence, or the handful in silence and the frankincense with an improper thought, רבי מאיר says it is פיגול and one gets כרת for eating it. חכמים say there is no כרת until he has the improper thought during the whole permitting act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא it began in step 12. This is the part that holds the real challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning a מנחה involves two items together, the קומץ and the לבונה, and together they are the מתיר that permits the rest of the מנחה. The ברייתא gives two orders: the thought on the first item only, or the thought on the second item only. רבי מאיר says פיגול in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: burning on the מזבח
the handful of flour taken from the מנחה
frankincense, burned together with the קומץ
in silence, meaning with no improper thought
the item or act that permits the offering to be eaten
spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for eating פיגול

phrases.english: But when he came to the burning,
if he placed the handful with an improper thought
and the frankincense in silence,
or he placed the handful in silence
and the frankincense with an improper thought,
Rabbi Meir says: it is piggul,
and one is liable to karet for it.
And the Sages say: there is no karet
unless he has the improper thought during the entire permitting act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that רבי מאיר does not allow פיגול through half a מתיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted case will show רבי מאיר ruling פיגול even when the thought came only during the second half.

steps.title: The challenge: the thought was only on the second item, and רבי מאיר still disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the second case: the handful was silent and only the frankincense had the thought, yet רבי מאיר still says פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches the handful in silence and the frankincense with an improper thought, and still רבי מאיר disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows exactly which line of the ברייתא causes the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case there was no improper thought before the frankincense, so the כהן was not continuing an earlier thought. If רבי מאיר still says פיגול, it seems he allows פיגול through half the מתיר. That contradicts the view that he does not.

keyTerms.meaning: in any case, it teaches
he disagrees

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
the handful in silence
and the frankincense with an improper thought, and he disagrees!
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר, who disagrees with חכמים and says it is פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 12-13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that, for רבי מאיר, half a מתיר alone cannot make פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There was no earlier thought to continue, so only half a מתיר had the thought, yet רבי מאיר says פיגול.

steps.title: Rereading the case: the frankincense with the thought came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading the ברייתא so that the frankincense, with the improper thought, was already burned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it means: he had already placed the frankincense with an improper thought, and then the handful in silence.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the challenged view by reading the second case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the frankincense with the thought was first, the silent handful afterward simply continues that thought. Then רבי מאיר's ruling of פיגול fits the 'continuing thought' explanation, not half a מתיר.

keyTerms.meaning: say, read it as
already

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: כְּבָר נָתַן אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה.
phrases.english: Say: he had already placed the frankincense with an improper thought.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: כְּבָר נָתַן אֶת הַלְּבוֹנָה בְּמַחְשָׁבָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the order of events in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thought came only on the second item, with no earlier thought.
steps.terutzMaskana: The thought came on the first item, and the second item simply continued it.

steps.title: Two problems with the rereading
steps.stepSummary: The rereading fails. It would make the second case the same as the first, and another ברייתא says outright 'and afterward' the frankincense was with the thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: First, that is just the first case again! And besides, another ברייתא teaches: 'and afterward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 15 with two arguments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the ברייתא's first case already covers a thought on the first item and silence on the second, so the rereading would make it say the same thing twice. Second, another ברייתא says clearly that the frankincense with the thought came 'afterward,' so the thought really was only on the second item.

keyTerms.meaning: one problem
the first part of the ברייתא
and furthermore
and afterward

phrases.english: One problem: that is the same as the first clause!
And furthermore, it is taught: "and afterward"!
phrases.notes: Another ברייתא says the frankincense with the thought came after the handful, so the rereading cannot work.

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the ברייתא repeat itself, and another ברייתא says the opposite order outright.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the difficulty remains unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer, so the challenge against the view stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view (ריש לקיש) that רבי מאיר never allows פיגול through half a מתיר stays challenged by this ברייתא. 'קשיא' means the question is left standing. It does not formally declare the view rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא shows רבי מאיר saying פיגול even when only the second half of the מתיר had the thought. This is left as a standing difficulty against the view that he needs a continuing thought.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is not the same as 'תיובתא.' It means the problem is left unresolved, not that the view is completely thrown out.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge once the answer of step 15 is rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge from the ברייתא stays unresolved.

steps.title: New משנה: items that carry no פיגול liability
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins, listing items for which one does not get כרת because of פיגול. It starts with the קומץ, the קטורת, and the לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These are the items for which one is not liable because of פיגול: the handful, the incense, and the frankincense,
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a list of items that are never subject to the כרת of פיגול. The list continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was how an offering becomes פיגול. Now the משנה lists items that cannot bring פיגול liability at all. The first three are all items burned on the מזבח: the handful, the incense, and the frankincense.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
the incense offering
an offering ruined by an improper thought about the time it would be eaten or burned

phrases.english: MISHNA:
And these are the items for which one is not liable
because of piggul:
the handful, the incense, and the frankincense,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no כרת of פיגול for the קומץ, the קטורת, or the לבונה, and the list continues.
